import functools
import subprocess


def factory(cmd):
    return functools.partial(subprocess.run, cmd)


argv = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-partialfixed-held"]
runner = factory(argv)
argv = ["pacman", "-Q", "r22-partialfixed-decoy"]
runner()
rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, static reasoning only (no execution, no measurement). functools.partial(subprocess.run, cmd) evaluates and stores its fixed argument objects at partial-construction time. The call factory(argv) binds parameter cmd to the list object ["pacman","-S","r22-partialfixed-held"] that argv referenced at factory-call time, and the returned partial holds that same object in its stored args. The later module-level statement argv = ["pacman","-Q","r22-partialfixed-decoy"] is a rebinding of the name argv to a fresh list object; rebinding a name never mutates a previously bound object, so the partial's stored argv is untouched. runner() therefore invokes subprocess.run(["pacman","-S","r22-partialfixed-held"]), yielding exactly one statically determined finding: host_mutation 'pacman -S r22-partialfixed-held', observed, with zero unparsed. A detector that evaluates the factory-call argument or the partial's fixed argument in the invocation environment instead of the creation environment (the F1 invoke-time-binding defect, extended to partial fixed arguments) resolves argv to the rebound decoy list and fabricates an observed 'pacman -Q r22-partialfixed-decoy' row while missing the true host_mutation; that command is forbidden as observed. All argv tokens are inert markers inside a subprocess.run call that is never executed by the wave.
